USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Acute ocular symptoms

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 58-year-old woman with previously identified untreated narrow anterior chamber angles starts bupropion. She develops severe unilateral eye pain, blurred vision, colored halos and nausea. Examination shows a red eye and a poorly reactive mid-dilated pupil. Which adverse event is most likely?

  1. Optic neuritis
  2. Retinal detachment
  3. Acute angle-closure glaucoma
  4. Chronic open-angle glaucoma
  5. Uncomplicated allergic conjunctivitis
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Acute angle-closure glaucoma

Drug-associated pupillary dilation can precipitate angle closure in a susceptible eye; this presentation needs urgent ophthalmic assessment.

Understanding the options

Acute angle-closure glaucoma
Drug-associated pupillary dilation can precipitate angle closure in a susceptible eye; this presentation needs urgent ophthalmic assessment.
Chronic open-angle glaucoma
It usually does not present as sudden painful visual loss with halos and nausea.
Uncomplicated allergic conjunctivitis
Itching and discharge would be more typical than severe pain and a mid-dilated pupil.
Optic neuritis
Pain with eye movement may occur, but the red eye and pupil findings favor angle closure.
Retinal detachment
Flashes, floaters and a curtain-like defect are more typical, usually without this painful red eye.
